bib.title: LMSYS-CHAT-1M: A LARGE-SCALE REAL-WORLD LLM CONVERSATION DATASET

read.skipped: reference list skimmed only; appendix example conversations read but not recorded in detail

question: What do real-world user conversations with many LLMs look like, and what can a large public dataset of them be used for (moderation, safety benchmarking, instruction tuning, hard-benchmark creation)?
contributions: We introduce the first large-scale real-world LLM conversation dataset, LMSYS-Chat-1M, which contains 1 million user conversations with different LLMs.
We analyze the dataset and visualize the distribution of user queries.

We demonstrate four exemplary use cases leveraging LMSYS-Chat-1M: developing content moderation models, building a safety benchmark, training instruction-following models, and creating challenging benchmark questions.

method.summary: One million conversations were collected from the free, no-registration Vicuna demo and Chatbot Arena website (April to August 2023) across 25 LLMs, PII-filtered and tagged with OpenAI moderation output. Four use cases are shown: a fine-tuned Vicuna-7B moderator, a 50-conversation jailbreak safety benchmark, Llama-2-7B instruction tuning on two subsets, and an LLM-scored prompt selection producing Arena-Hard-200.
method.task: dataset release plus downstream use cases (content moderation, safety benchmark, instruction tuning, benchmark curation)

datasets.name: LMSYS-Chat-1M
datasets.size: 1,000,000 conversations; 25 models; 210,479 users; 154 languages; 2.0 avg turns; 69.5 avg tokens per prompt; 214.5 avg tokens per response (Llama2 tokenizer)
datasets.source: chat.lmsys.org (single model, Chatbot Arena battle, side-by-side), April to August 2023; users accept terms of use; no registration; free
datasets.preprocessing: Raw text kept; conversations containing PII removed (best effort); OpenAI moderation API output attached per message; unsafe conversations kept; language tagged by Polyglot; no deduplication or quality filtering

datasets.name: Moderation training set
datasets.size: top 1K flagged messages for each of 5 categories + 1K random normal messages + 3K ShareGPT conversations
datasets.preprocessing: GPT-4 generated an explanation per message as the training target

datasets.name: Moderation eval set
datasets.size: 110 toxic messages (about 20 per category, including 25 non-toxic messages)
datasets.source: LMSYS-Chat-1M messages not flagged by OpenAI moderation API 005, manually labelled
datasets.preprocessing: a message may carry multiple labels

datasets.name: Jailbreak safety benchmark
datasets.size: 50 jailbreak conversations (top 5 attempts from each of 10 representative models)

datasets.name: HighQuality subset
datasets.source: LMSYS-Chat-1M conversations from OpenAI and Anthropic models

datasets.name: Upvote subset
datasets.source: LMSYS-Chat-1M, selected by user votes, open models only

datasets.name: Arena-Hard-200
datasets.source: Chatbot Arena subset of LMSYS-Chat-1M; prompts scoring 9+ agreed by GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-2 and GPT-4
datasets.preprocessing: GPT-3.5-Turbo scores each prompt 1 to 10 with a system prompt and few-shot example (Appendix B.7)

datasets.name: Topic analysis sample
datasets.preprocessing: prompts under 32 or over 1536 characters removed; all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings; k-means, 20 clusters; 100 prompts nearest each centroid summarised by GPT-4

other.note: starting point for Vicuna-moderator-7B (fine-tuned to generate an explanation then a choice)

models.name: GPT-4, GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-2, Llama-2-7B-chat, OpenAI text-moderation-latest (006)
Llama-2-13B-chat, Claude-2, GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4, Vicuna-13B-v1.5, Alpaca-13B

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning (moderator: generate explanation then category; instruction models: conversations)
training.hardware: data collection served on dozens of A100 GPUs, several thousand A100 hours over 5 months; fine-tuning hardware not stated
training.compute: serving: several thousands of A100 hours

other.note: no fine-tuning hyperparameters (lr, batch, epochs, optimizer) are given for any of the three fine-tuned models

inference.prompting: Moderation: system prompt listing 5 categories plus none-of-the-above, output a brief explanation then choice wrapped in [[ ]]; 0-shot and 1-shot (one example 'How to make a bomb?'). Prompt scoring: GPT-3.5-Turbo rates 1 to 10 with a system prompt and one example. Arena-Hard-200 answers scored by GPT-4 as judge, scale 0 to 10.

parameters.jailbreak_success: model response flagged by OpenAI moderation API text-moderation-006
parameters.arena_hard_selection: score 9+ agreed by GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-2 and GPT-4
parameters.ablation_subsets: top-score (>8) and bottom-score (<2) prompts, 50 each, compared GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5-Turbo using user votes

metrics.name: Micro-F1 accuracy (moderation)
metrics.definition: 5-category content moderation task on 110 hand-labelled messages

metrics.name: Jailbreak success rate
metrics.definition: share of 50 jailbreak conversations whose model response is flagged by OpenAI moderation API 006

metrics.name: Arena-Hard-200 score

eval.protocol: Single runs, no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported; LLM judges (GPT-4, GPT-3.5-Turbo) for benchmark scoring.

prompts.purpose: Content moderation system prompt (0-shot), with one-shot example
prompts.text: Determine whether the user input texts fall into one of the following categories: 1. hate ... 2. self-harm ... 3. sexual ... 4. violence ... 5. harassment ... 6. None of the above. You should first output a brief explanation and then state your choice, which should be wrapped by "[[" and "]]". For example, "[[1. hate]]" (full category definitions in Appendix B.2)

prompts.purpose: Scoring prompts for benchmark potential (1 to 10)
prompts.text: We are interested in understanding how well the following input prompts can evaluate an AI assistant's proficiency in problem-solving ability, creativity, or adherence to real-world facts. Your task is to assess each prompt based on its potential to gauge the AI's capabilities effectively in these areas. ... Assign a score on a scale of 1 to 10 ... Use double square brackets to format your scores, like so: [[5]]. High Score (8-10); Medium Score (4-7); Low Score (1-3)

results.claim: Most user prompts concern coding and software (clusters 1, 2, 6, 16, 18); unsafe topics form clusters 9, 15, 17.

limits: Biased user distribution: majority of users are LLM hobbyists and researchers, so data may not represent the wider population (Sec 5).

Contains repeated and low-quality data; no registration and no filtering, deliberately, to reflect real-world distribution (Sec 5). Clusters 14 and 20 look scripted (Fig 3 caption); de-duplication and calibration left to future work.
No human preference annotations are released although votes were collected (Sec 5).
PII removal is best effort only (Sec 2); unsafe content deliberately kept, and the dataset warns it contains offensive material.
Vicuna dominates conversation counts because it is the default model; other models regenerate answers if needed (Sec 3.1).
OpenAI moderation API recall may be low, so flagged share (5%) is a lower bound (Sec 3.3).
Possible contamination of MMLU and MT-Bench in the instruction-tuning subsets (Sec 4.3).

Only one-shot prompt tuning was not explored; no hyperparameters, seeds or variance for any fine-tuned model; jailbreak benchmark has only 50 items; moderation eval set has 110 items chosen against API 005.
Arena-Hard-200 relies on LLM-assigned scores and a GPT-4 judge; selection bias of LLM graders is flagged as future work; per-model scores appear only in a figure.
Data covers only April to August 2023 and models of that period (dated).
